clips.title: The story
paras: Naga now threaten Ashenvale from the Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar sends Alliance champions to scour the northwestern coast, where an ancient ruined city lies. Stopping the naga protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves’ distant past.

At Ashenvale’s northwestern edge, the Zoram Strand meets the Veiled Sea. Its shore lies northwest of Astranaar, where the forest canopy gives way to the coast. The beach was quiet for ages, its stones left from a civilization shattered ten millennia ago. Now Wrathtail naga have come out of the dark tides in force. They have made a hostile beachhead on the borders of night elven territory, and threaten to press inland.

The city of Zoram lies shattered beneath the surf, submerged during the Great Sundering. For ages, it remained abandoned and nearly forgotten by the kaldorei. The naga’s sudden arrival among its ruins stirs bitter memories among Astranaar’s defenders. Sentinels such as Shindrell Swiftfire know the invaders as twisted cousins, born of their own ancient catastrophe. They will not let the depths claim the shore again.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: There is evil lurking on our northwestern coast, known as the Zoram Strand.
It is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram, destroyed during the Sundering and submerged beneath the seas. It has been lost to the night elves for ages. Lost, and nearly forgotten.
Now, the naga have returned, and for what reason we do not know. But reason matters little; we must slay these fiends and throw them back to the depths!
Return to me when your mission is complete.

clips.title: Progress
paras: We cannot allow the naga to invade our coasts, friend. It is vital that you go to the Zoram Strand and complete your mission.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Very well done, friend. Your actions in the Zoram Strand against the naga are commendable.
I know your feat was not easily accomplished, for the strength and guile of the naga is well known to the night elves. We know this, for we share a history with them.
It is a history I care not to repeat.
